sections.changelog:
Added

  • Self-contained `object-cache.php` drop-in with generation-based flush, so a cache reset never touches neighbouring sites on a shared Memcached server.
  • Three-level diagnosis on the plugin page: PHP extension, server connection, set/get/delete round trip.
  • Connection test with value verification and a shared-server notice based on `curr_items`.
  • Automatic detection of typical hosts, ports and Unix sockets.
  • Enable, update and disable buttons for the drop-in, with an outdated-drop-in banner after plugin updates.
  • Detection of third-party drop-ins (W3 Total Cache, Redis Object Cache, LiteSpeed and others) — the file is never overwritten.
  • Unique key prefix generated from the database name, table prefix and a random salt.
  • Automatic non-persistent groups for WooCommerce: sessions, rate limits, coupons, product and order objects.
  • Optional SASL credentials, custom key prefix and extra non-persistent groups under Advanced.
  • Site Health test and debug information section.
  • WP-CLI commands: `status`, `test`, `enable`, `disable`, `flush`.
  • Admin bar entry for flushing the cache.
  • Emergency `MVWEB_MC_DISABLE` constant and wp-config overrides for host, port, prefix and SASL credentials.
  • Day-long TTL ceiling for entries WordPress stores without an expiry, so a Memcached outage cannot leave stale values in the cache forever.
  • Outage marker with an admin banner offering a cache flush once the server is back.
  • Russian translation.
  • Enabling the cache starts a new key generation, so data cached before the cache was switched off can never resurface — without it, turning the cache back on could roll the site back to an older snapshot of its options, down to losing recently activated plugins.
  • Values stored through the legacy extension are wrapped in an envelope, so a cached `false` is no longer indistinguishable from a cache miss.
  • Support for the legacy `memcache` extension alongside `memcached`, picked automatically — mass hosting such as Beget ships only the old one, so the plugin now works there without a support ticket.

Fixed

  • Entries with an expiry over 30 days are now stored as an absolute timestamp, as the Memcached protocol requires — previously they expired instantly (WordPress and WooCommerce store year-long transients).
  • The generation counter is no longer reset to 1 when the server fails to answer, which used to undo every earlier cache flush after a transient network error.
  • `decr()` now uses the atomic `Memcached::decrement()` like `incr()` does, so concurrent decrements no longer lose updates (WooCommerce decrements order, product and review counters).
  • `replace()` distinguishes a cached `false` from a missing key.
  • `add()` reports failure when the server refuses the write, so the common "successful add means lock acquired" pattern cannot get a false positive.
  • `delete()` returns the real result instead of always `true`, matching core behaviour.
  • `flush()` reports failure when the generation counter could not be written.
  • `flush_group()` only clears the request-level cache for non-persistent groups, so `wp_cache_flush_group( 'coupons' )` from WooCommerce no longer wipes the whole site cache.
  • Keys are validated like core does — an empty key is rejected instead of colliding with other empty keys.
  • `wp_cache_reset()` is defined again; core declares it in the file the drop-in replaces, and legacy callers used to hit a fatal error.
  • The drop-in reuses a persistent connection keyed by host, port and prefix instead of reconnecting on every request.
  • Plugin settings are memoised per request: reading them repeatedly costs one query instead of one per call.
